# `acknowledgement-not-owner`

An acknowledgement's owner doesn't own the finding

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `acknowledgement-not-owner` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M9) |
| **Group** | Spec and engine notices ([RULES.md section 11](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

With `acknowledgements.require-owner: true` in the policy, an acknowledgement whose `owner` isn't one of the finding's owners (or that has no `owner`) doesn't apply: the finding counts as if it weren't acknowledged.

## Why this default

Notice only: it explains why an acknowledged finding still counts. Only a team that owns the affected operations should accept a change to them.

## Example

From test case [`acknowledgement-not-owner`](../../test/cases/acknowledgement-not-owner/): With acknowledgements.require-owner, only an owner of the finding can acknowledge it. The removed operation is owned by @pets-team (x-owner on its path item), but the acknowledgement is by @platform, so it doesn't apply: the removal still counts as breaking, and acknowledgement-not-owner says why.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-   '/pets/{id}':
-     x-owner: '@pets-team'
-     delete:
-       responses:
-         '200':
-           description: ok
```

Findings:

- `operation-removed` · error · DELETE /pets/{id}
- `acknowledgement-not-owner` · info · DELETE /pets/{id}

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  acknowledgement-not-owner: info
```

## How to fix

Have an owner of the finding acknowledge it (set `owner` to one of the teams listed), or fix the finding's owners (`x-owner` or `owners.assign`).
